content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents an approach for transfer learning in the model based reinforcement learning. The approach is modular, can utilize multiple source tasks, and can transfer parameters partially. In addition, it introduces "meta-model transfer learning" which is essentially a network that takes as input predictions of model components trained on source tasks to make its own predictions in turn.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
+
The paper is clearly written and easy to follow. The contributions are well defined and scoped out in relation to literature. The approach  combines many different good ideas into a novel transfer learning strategy. Experiments are well thought out and comparison is done to non-transfer learning baseline.

-
Some of the method details are under explained and seem arbitrarily selected. Such as why an additive model was used for fractional transfer learning and not other possibilities such as random reinitialization of neurons. 
Related to above, ablations need to be performed on the different components of the approach to show which has the greatest impact on transfer.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is pretty clearly written, of high quality and is novel. There are high level descriptions of training procedures and details for experiments provided in Section 5. There is a link to code which was not verified.
content.summary_of_the_review: In summary, with a better motivation for some design choices of transfer components and ablations of them to determine their importance, this could be a good contribution to ICLR.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper builds on top of Dreamer, uses it for multi-task training, then transfers to the target task via a fraction of initialized parameters or freezing&reusing techniques. Experiments are conducted on deepmind control suits.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
I did not see obvious strengths in this paper.

Weaknesses:

This paper is a composition of three existing methods (techniques): Dreamer, parameter fusion, and SEER, which makes the novelty of this paper trivial.

The motivation for why considering an MBRL in transfer settings is not provided. 

Furthermore, using one model to learn multiple tasks' dynamics without any modifications compared with vanilla Dreamer is not convincing.

A lot of details are missing, for example, sec 4.1.3 mentioned 'initial experiments' which is not included in the paper, nor the appendix.

The literature review on multiple-source policy transfer is not extensive [1-3].

[1] Multipolar: Multi-source policy aggregation for transfer reinforcement learning between diverse environmental dynamics.
[2] Efficient deep reinforcement learning via adaptive policy transfer.
[3] Multi-policy Grounding and Ensemble Policy Learning for Transfer Learning with Dynamics Mismatch.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The clarity of this paper should be improved, e.g., grammar issues and a lot of details.

The novelty is very limited, as listed in the pros and cons part.

The authors provide the open-sourced code.

One thing is that this paper seems to use an incorrect LaTeX template.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper needs to be further improved in its methodology, what's the contribution and why it is important are not clear. This paper also needs a careful literature review and experimental comparison to make it solid. The current version is not ready to be accepted. Overall, I recommend rejecting this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a transfer learning method to transfer from models/policies trained on multiple sources to target task. This multi source transfer learning approach is applied to Dreamer and evaluated on multiple mujoco based environments. Results show improved transfer performance on the evaluation tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

This paper tackles the difficult challenge of transfer learning in reinforcement learning
The empirical evaluation is solid and consider many different environment

Weaknesses:

Overall it is difficult what is the main the contribution of the paper.
The meta model trasnfer learning approach presented in section 4.2.2 simply concatenates the previously trained networks. This is similar to the approach followed by other transfer learning algorithms such as progressive nets. The issue with these approaches is that computation scales linearly with the number of tasks which is undesirable.
Similarly the fractional transfer learning method presented in section 4.1.2 is pretty much the shrink and perturb method presented in [1]

[1] On Warm-Starting Neural Network Training, Ash & Adams, 2020
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
I found the paper difficult to follow, particularly section 4.
Providing pseudo code for the algorithm and plots / figures would be helpful to understand the paper more easily.
content.summary_of_the_review: Given the similarity between this paper and existing approaches for multi task learning in the literature the contribution of the paper does not seem sufficient for publication in its current state.

content.title: Multi-Source Transfer Learning for Deep Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
content.abstract: A crucial challenge in reinforcement learning is to reduce the number of interactions with the environment that an agent requires to master a given task. Transfer learning proposes to address this issue by re-using knowledge from previously learned tasks. However, determining which source task qualifies as optimal for knowledge extraction, as well as the choice regarding which algorithm components to transfer, represent severe obstacles to its application in reinforcement learning. The goal of this paper is to alleviate these issues with modular multi-source transfer learning techniques. Our proposed methodologies automatically learn how to extract useful information from source tasks, regardless of the difference in state-action space and reward function. We support our claims with extensive and challenging cross-domain experiments for visual control.
